Consequently a prime-degree field stabilizer and an exchanged-pair stabilizer are maximal; for a compositum of two prime degrees its maximal overgroups can only be the stabilizers of its prime-degree subfields.
  - Explanation: Explains Proposition 36, proving that proper overgroups of field stabilizers preserve subfields and overgroups of paired stabilizers preserve the pair, guaranteeing maximality in prime degree.
- **stmt-fb-canonical-quadratic-exclusion** (theorem, [source](#stmt-fb-canonical-quadratic-exclusion)): In the prepared symplectic configuration in characteristic two, replicated failures whose full stabilizers preserve canonical quadratics with the ambient polar form are impossible. This excludes ordered tensor stabilizers with alternating factor forms, nontrivial-adjoint field stabilizers, and exchanged pair stabilizers as soon as the common previous-good label is irreducible.
  - Explanation: Explains Lemma 69, excluding stabilizers that preserve canonical quadratics in symplectic characteristic two using the irreducibility of a common previous-good label.
- **stmt-fb-both-high-factors** (theorem, [source](#stmt-fb-both-high-factors)): At the present forward-test stage, a homogeneous family of failures preserving proper ordered matrix tensor factorizations cannot have both factor degrees above the fixed large-degree threshold. In isometry types the factors are selfadjoint and have the normalized factor forms.
  - Explanation: Explains Proposition 37, excluding homogeneous failure families preserving ordered tensor factorizations whenever both factor degrees exceed the large-degree threshold.
- **stmt-fb-nuisance-planes** (theorem, [source](#stmt-fb-nuisance-planes)): After [fb:both-high-factors](#fb:both-high-factors), the missing side of an ordered-factor failure has large degree. Its retained side can only be a linear plane over $\mathbf F_2$, an odd-characteristic bilateral orthogonal plane, or a symplectic plane over $\mathbf F_2$.
  - Explanation: Explains Lemma 70, narrowing the remaining ordered-factor possibilities to configurations where the retained side is one of three specific nuisance planes.
- **stmt-fb-large-transfer** (bound, [source](#stmt-fb-large-transfer)): For the prime-field witnesses in this round, the transferred natural degree exceeds any prescribed absolute bound after the earlier missing-site tests have been enlarged. The same conclusion holds at the full simultaneous field or paired stabilizers used below, relative to their lower endpoint $g_*$. Prime-field labels are coatoms. Two disjoint witnesses whose fields commute cannot have a field compositum.
  - Explanation: Explains Lemma 71, establishing that transferred degree bounds force prime-field labels to be coatoms and preclude field composita for commuting disjoint witnesses.
- **stmt-fb-field-pair-exclusion** (theorem, [source](#stmt-fb-field-pair-exclusion)): In the prepared forward-test configuration, the prime-field and exchanged-pair failures are impossible. The nuisance planes of [fb:nuisance-planes](#fb:nuisance-planes) are therefore impossible as well, completing the ordered-factor exclusion.
  - Explanation: Explains Proposition 38, ruling out prime fields, exchanged pairs, and nuisance planes to finalize the exclusion of all ordered tensor factorizations.
- **stmt-fb-tensor-merging** (theorem, [source](#stmt-fb-tensor-merging)): Consider compatible sets of tensor directions $A B$ and $B C$ in the prepared classical configuration, with common aggregate degree $\dim B$ sufficiently large. Suppose their tensor-supported natural special groups are available. They generate a group containing the tensor-supported special on $A B C$. In orthogonal characteristic two, use the canonical orthogonal special on every subset with at least two slots, with product polar form and quadratic zero on fine simple tensors. Symplectic characteristic two has already been excluded by [fb:canonical-quadratic-exclusion](#fb:canonical-quadratic-exclusion).
  - Explanation: Explains that when two compatible sets of tensor factor directions overlap on a shared tensor direction B of sufficiently large dimension, their corresponding natural special subgroups generate the full natural special group acting on the combined tensor product space A ⊗ B ⊗ C.
- **stmt-fb-permuted-tensors** (theorem, [source](#stmt-fb-permuted-tensors)): After the preceding rounds, neither a full-algebra elementary abelian normalizer nor a nontrivial permuted tensor-system stabilizer can be a failure label in the forward test.
  - Explanation: Shows that stabilizers of tensor decompositions subject to coordinate permutations cannot occur as failure labels in the forward marker test, since their common matrix refinements and column alterations force a join generating the full ancestor simple group.
- **stmt-fb-grounding** (bound, [source](#stmt-fb-grounding)): After the prescribed rounds, every tested descendant has an actual nested normal simple supplement with soluble centralizer in the base. Relative to a high classical ancestor it is absolutely irreducible and avoids all the excluded tensor structures. Relative to an alternating ancestor it is primitive and transitive unless the desired point configuration has already been obtained. Its simple type can be required to exceed any fixed bounded order or bounded-rank threshold.* *The same actual normal simplicity and full spanning apply to a label above a previous-good axis and below the ancestor when it has the indicated nonabelian part: either a contained perfect simple group as used here, or its own pure link satisfying the normal test. In the first case that perfect group lies in the resulting normal simple.
  - Explanation: Demonstrates that eliminating abelian normalizers and tensor systems guarantees that any tested descendant label contains an actual nested nonabelian simple normal subgroup acting irreducibly, whose centralizer in the base group is soluble.
- **stmt-fb-protection-count** (theorem, [source](#stmt-fb-protection-count)): With the bounded predicates homogenized relative to the allowed ordered prefixes, choose trial increments $a<b$ of matching continuation color and with $b$ sufficiently large compared with $(\|W\|+a)^4$. If a protection failure survives at a continuing trial extension, then one obtains arbitrarily many coatom witnesses on distinct singleton positions, of the same protection kind, corresponding to distinct primes. All these witnesses are counted for one fixed later descendant $B_U$.
  - Explanation: Establishes that any persistent failure of run protections (either tensor coarsening or field roots) can be homogenized and reduced to an unbounded family of distinct coatom witnesses omitting single coordinate positions across distinct prime parameters.
- **stmt-fb-singleton-roots** (theorem, [source](#stmt-fb-singleton-roots)): The singleton coatom witnesses in [fb:protection-count](#fb:protection-count) cannot be normalizers of fixing prime roots.
  - Explanation: Rules out field automorphisms of prime degree as singleton coatom failures by demonstrating that their combined fixed subgroup would force the third coatom simple factor to be a proper subfield group that already normalizes one of the individual root simples.
- **stmt-fb-sparse-weight** (theorem, [source](#stmt-fb-sparse-weight)): In this configuration, $B$ is high classical in the same characteristic, with natural dimension $w\ge m$. Its action on $V$ has highest weight $p^x\lambda$, where $\lambda\ne0$ is $p$-restricted. Every active type-A node of $\lambda$ defines a cut whose smaller side has fewer than $2d$ entries. In a signed type, its dominant word has fewer than $2d$ nonzero coordinates and has no spin support.
  - Explanation: Proves that the normal simple subgroup B extracted from the third coatom must be of high classical type in the same characteristic, and that the highest weight of its representation on the ambient module V is extremely sparse relative to its rank.
- **stmt-fb-natural-restriction** (theorem, [source](#stmt-fb-natural-restriction)): Under the preceding hypotheses, the projective natural $B$-module remains irreducible on the finite group $Y$ over the algebraic closure.
  - Explanation: Establishes that the natural representation of B cannot decompose into proper parabolics, nondegenerate submodules, or singular lines when restricted to the subgroup Y, thereby proving that the restriction remains irreducible.
- **stmt-fb-rational-lift** (theorem, [source](#stmt-fb-rational-lift)): The restriction in [fb:natural-restriction](#fb:natural-restriction) is the restriction of a parameter-restricted rational irreducible of the simply connected algebraic group of $Y$, of highest weight $\eta$. It gives a morphism into the simply connected algebraic group of $B$, preserving the required forms. The rational composition with $L_B(p^x\lambda)$ is irreducible. After removing the common scale $p^x$, its highest weight $\mu$ has a single natural or dual-natural coefficient one at each nonzero digit.
  - Explanation: Lifts the finite group representation to a rational morphism of simply connected algebraic groups and proves that composing this morphism with the highest-weight representation of B yields an irreducible rational module whose highest weight digits are singleton natural or dual-natural weights.
- **stmt-fb-endpoint-cuts** (theorem, [source](#stmt-fb-endpoint-cuts)): In this same configuration, $\lambda$ is supported only at the two endpoints in type A, or at the first node in a signed type.
  - Explanation: Applies a universal cut argument on the weight multiset to show that small subset invariance under the intermediate Weyl reflections restricts the support of the highest weight λ strictly to the diagram endpoints or the first node.
- **stmt-fb-natural-recognition** (theorem, [source](#stmt-fb-natural-recognition)): In the tensor-coarsening configuration above, $\lambda$ is a natural weight, up to duality. Consequently $w=v$, and $B$ acts naturally on $V$, up to Frobenius twist.
  - Explanation: Analyzes weight collisions and PBW multiplicity bounds to eliminate coefficients strictly greater than one or supported on multiple endpoints, proving that λ is the first fundamental weight and that B acts via its standard natural representation.
- **stmt-fb-singleton-tensors** (theorem, [source](#stmt-fb-singleton-tensors)): The singleton coatom witnesses in [fb:protection-count](#fb:protection-count) cannot be prime tensor-coarsening stabilizers.
  - Explanation: Excludes prime tensor coarsenings as singleton coatom witnesses because natural recognition forces B to be fixed by a field automorphism of strictly smaller height, which would shift the non-zero digit support modulo the period.
- **stmt-fb-forward-completion** (theorem, [source](#stmt-fb-forward-completion)): The forward marker assertion of [r:forward-marker](#r:forward-marker) holds. In the prepared configuration, the assumption of no point success at all the prescribed bounded prefixes is impossible once the initial marker set is sufficiently large.
  - Explanation: Concludes the forward marker argument by demonstrating that an absence of point success would produce a descending chain of nested simple subgroups exceeding the absolute path-length bound D_0.
- **stmt-t-weighted-labels** (theorem, [source](#stmt-t-weighted-labels)): The labels in [t:weighted-template](#t:weighted-template) are exactly the overgroups in $F$. Its coatoms are the labels $C_D$ below. Absorption in a join follows residual orbits. Axis filters and axis ideals again give the weighted templates on the units that remain.
  - Explanation: Identifies the complete lattice of overgroups in F as pairs of absorbed unit footprints and subgroup restraints, characterizing the lattice coatoms and proving that joins correspond to the orbit absorption of units into the foundation.
- **stmt-t-weighted-footprint** (theorem, [source](#stmt-t-weighted-footprint)): In every nontrivial lattice image $\bar F$, the footprint is well defined. All cut coatoms survive distinctly and are all the coatoms of the image. Residual orbit discrepancies are detected by absorption. The pure marker links, and canonical permutation intervals on copies of any fixed package of units, are faithful.
  - Explanation: Establishes footprints and faithful pure links in the stated setting.
- **stmt-t-weighted-algebra** (theorem, [source](#stmt-t-weighted-algebra)): Every nilpotent join-preserving deflation of $\bar F$ is zero. If some nontrivial image of $F$ is the congruence lattice of a finite algebra of size $m$, there is an ordinary finite-group interval representing the dual of a nontrivial image of $F$, whose top group has order at most $60^m m!$. The full lattice $F$ itself has a finite algebra representation.
  - Explanation: Establishes from algebras to ordinary intervals in the stated setting.
- **stmt-t-weighted-normal-test** (theorem, [source](#stmt-t-weighted-normal-test)): A normal-multiple label cannot satisfy $$e\wedge b\le a<b\le e\vee a.$$ Its axis projections are again normal-multiple labels. If $L$ is minimal normal and nontrivial, a nontrivial proper intersection $L\cap G_b$ cannot be normalized at a family of labels whose actual groups generate $G$. The equations in the proof test precisely the normalizations needed below.
  - Explanation: Establishes projection and intersection tests for normals in the stated setting.
- **stmt-t-weighted-normal-internal** (theorem, [source](#stmt-t-weighted-normal-internal)): If $e$ is a proper nonendpoint normal-multiple label, then $I(e)=\emptyset$ and $e\le J^*$. The conclusion remains available after any of the bounded axis restrictions used in the proof, and when all unit actions are replaced by full symmetric groups.
  - Explanation: Establishes a proper normal label is internal in the stated setting.
- **stmt-t-weighted-normal-parallel** (theorem, [source](#stmt-t-weighted-normal-parallel)): After quotienting by the base core, suppose that a minimal nontrivial normal subgroup gives a proper nonendpoint label $e$. Let $B$ be the intersection of $J^*$ with all full symmetric parallel-block labels. Then $e\le B$. This case is impossible in reverse orientation. In forward orientation $[0,B]$ is the exact lattice of subspaces of the sign space having two coordinates for each primary square.
  - Explanation: Establishes parallel restrictions on an internal normal in the stated setting.
- **stmt-t-weighted-normal** (theorem, [source](#stmt-t-weighted-normal)): For sufficiently large absolute cohort stock, every ordinary interval representing a nontrivial weighted image, in either orientation, satisfies $(*)$. Its base acts transitively on the simple factors of its monolith modulo the base core. The same assertion holds for the bounded axis deletions used here, provided the remaining stock is sufficient.
  - Explanation: Establishes normal endpoint property for weighted images in the stated setting.
- **stmt-t-weighted-forward-projections** (theorem, [source](#stmt-t-weighted-forward-projections)): In a forward realization $[P,\mathcal W]^H$, suppose $P>1$ and $c(P)<\mathcal W$. Every cut coatom is a product label. If $P<c(P)$, its closure label has empty footprint and lies below $J^*$.
  - Explanation: Establishes forward proper projections in the stated setting.
- **stmt-t-weighted-copy-action** (theorem, [source](#stmt-t-weighted-copy-action)): In a reverse invariant realization with $P>1$, let $z$ canonically permute $k$ identical nonempty packages of units, acting as the prescribed bottom inside each package. For a sufficiently large absolute $k$, $K_z$ is subdirect. The same holds for its canonical alternating-copy label once that label is sufficiently large.
  - Explanation: Establishes subdirect copy actions in reverse orientation in the stated setting.
- **stmt-t-weighted-small-labels** (theorem, [source](#stmt-t-weighted-small-labels)): Suppose $P>1$ in reverse orientation and $K_p=c(P)<\mathcal W$. Then $I(p)=\emptyset$, and every label supported on any fixed bounded number of units is subdirect. For the subsequent tests, a support bound of ten is enough. The required cohort stock is absolute.
  - Explanation: Establishes small labels are subdirect in the reverse proper-closure case in the stated setting.
- **stmt-t-weighted-residual-obstruction** (theorem, [source](#stmt-t-weighted-residual-obstruction)): Suppose all labels on the bounded supports used below are subdirect in a reverse realization. There is no nontrivial proper product actual group whose parameter label $p$ has empty footprint. This assertion applies both when $P>1$ and when $P=1$.
  - Explanation: Establishes residual products are impossible in reverse orientation in the stated setting.
- **stmt-t-weighted-reverse-projections** (theorem, [source](#stmt-t-weighted-reverse-projections)): In reverse orientation, if $P>1$, then $c(P)=\mathcal W$. If $P=1$, every nonidentity actual label is subdirect and the site-action image $\Lambda$ contains the inner automorphisms of $S$. In forward orientation with $P=1$, either a marker axis filter gives product success, or the same subdirectness and inner-action conclusions hold.
  - Explanation: Establishes reverse projections and the trivial-base cases in the stated setting.
- **stmt-t-weighted-product-success** (theorem, [source](#stmt-t-weighted-product-success)): There are absolute stock and marker-loss bounds with the following property. Any ordinary realization, in either orientation, of a nontrivial weighted image yields a forward realization of a nontrivial image of the weighted template with at most boundedly many markers deleted, in which product success holds. The stock bound is independent of all numerical unit sizes and of the number of cohorts. The simple group at a site has order at most the original top-group order. A larger prescribed fixed stock can be retained by increasing the initial absolute stock.
  - Explanation: Establishes product success with absolute stock in the stated setting.
- **stmt-t-weighted-restart** (theorem, [source](#stmt-t-weighted-restart)): From product success one obtains, after boundedly many further marker deletions, an actual power $A_\Omega^s$ with transitive operator action, base intersection $H\cap A_\Omega^s$, and product subgroups at every cut. The degree is high, and at least forty specified surviving marker cuts are genuine distinct alternating point stabilizers at each site. All previously product labels below the new top remain products.
  - Explanation: Establishes restart in an actual alternating power in the stated setting.
- **stmt-t-weighted-cuts** (theorem, [source](#stmt-t-weighted-cuts)): In the alternating realization of [t:weighted-restart](#t:weighted-restart), every cut coatom has site group the alternating intersection of a full subset stabilizer on $\Omega$. The two parts of this subset cut have unequal sizes. The ordinary site groups obtained by multiplication by $\Theta$ respect all cut intersections and the indicated covers.
  - Explanation: Establishes all cuts are full nonhalf subset stabilizers in the stated setting.
- **stmt-t-weighted-alignment** (theorem, [source](#stmt-t-weighted-alignment)): There is a single bijection from the formal units together with the foundation position to the $\Theta$-orbits on $\Omega$, under which every cut and every intersection of cuts is the corresponding stabilizer of unions of those orbits. Write $u_j>0$ for the size of the cell of unit $j$. The specified genuine point markers have size one.
  - Explanation: Establishes a uniform coordinate identification matching abstract lattice units and cuts to permutation orbit stabilizers on the underlying carrier set.
- **stmt-t-weighted-equal-totals** (theorem, [source](#stmt-t-weighted-equal-totals)): Let $D,E$ be disjoint bounded collections of nonfoundation units with equal formal total size, with ample spare markers outside them. If at least one of $D,E$ contains more than one unit, then $$\sum_{j\in D}u_j=\sum_{j\in E}u_j.$$ In a sufficiently numerous cohort, all copies have the same actual cell size. In particular, all surviving markers have size one.
  - Explanation: Proves that formal numerical equality of unit collections forces exact equality of actual orbit sizes through non-normal covering relations and wreath product labels.
- **stmt-t-weighted-square** (theorem, [source](#stmt-t-weighted-square)): For a primary square $O$ and its full side reference $R$, let $r=u_R$ in the alignment of [t:weighted-alignment](#t:weighted-alignment). If $r$ is even and $r\ge8$, then $u_O=r^2$.
  - Explanation: Demonstrates that parallel line systems and sign-graph homomorphisms force a primary square cell to have cardinality exactly equal to the square of its reference side.
- **stmt-t-weighted-realization** (theorem, [source](#stmt-t-weighted-realization)): Fix any bounded support size for the comparisons and any desired fixed number of spare copies. There are absolute initial cohort-stock and marker-loss bounds, independent of the numerical unit sizes and the number of cohorts, with the following property. The bounds may depend on the fixed support and spare-copy requirements. An ordinary realization of a nontrivial weighted image, in either orientation and with top order $M$, gives a forward realization after at most that many marker deletions, with all cuts product in an actual alternating power. A single common cell alignment gives positive sizes $u_j\le M$, equal on each cohort and one on all surviving markers. In this same alignment the equal-total reading of [t:weighted-equal-totals](#t:weighted-equal-totals) and the square reading of [t:weighted-square](#t:weighted-square) hold.* *If the input is a finite algebra of size $m$ representing a nontrivial image, the same conclusion holds with $M=60^m m!$, for a possibly different nontrivial image of the original template. The full template itself is finitely representable.
  - Explanation: Guarantees that nontrivial weighted images admit realizations with simultaneous numerical readings, preserving cell alignments and carrier size bounds.
- **stmt-n-compression** (bound, [source](#stmt-n-compression)): Let $X$ be a rank-one control of complexity at most $s$ on $I$, and let $D$ be a finite group of order at most $a$. There are computable bounds, depending only on $(s,a)$, for the following quantities:* 1. *the number of $X$-invariant subgroups $J\le D^I$;* 2. *the number of $X$-invariant right or left cosets of each such $J$;* 3. *the number of tuples needed to generate $J$ under the action of $X$, each of which can be chosen fixed by a trimmed control of bounded complexity.* *Every invariant coset has a representative fixed by such a trimmed control. No commutativity assumption on $D$ is required.
  - Explanation: Shows that coordinate values of invariant subgroups stabilize across large alphabets, bounding subgroup and coset counts computably in the base group order and complexity.
- **stmt-n-lifting** (bound, [source](#stmt-n-lifting)): Let $X$ be a rank-one control of complexity at most $s$ on $I$, let $D$ have bounded order, and let $U'\le S_I$ contain $X$. Suppose $U'$ is generated over $X$ by a bounded list of elements $g$ such that each $X\cap gXg^{-1}$ contains a rank-one control of bounded complexity. Then the number of subgroups $$V\le D^I\rtimes U',\qquad \operatorname{proj}(V)=U', \qquad (1,X)\le V,$$ is bounded computably in $s$ and these parameters. If $[U':\langle X^{U'}\rangle]$ is bounded, then so is $[V:\langle(1,X)^V\rangle]$.* *In the permutation action with bounded fibers, each such $V$ is generated over its pure copy of $X$ by boundedly many elements whose intersections with that pure control contain rank-one controls of bounded complexity on the expanded point set.
  - Explanation: Lifts subgroup enumeration bounds from base permutation actions to bounded extensions using coset compression over fiber groups.
- **stmt-n-primitive-parts** (theorem, [source](#stmt-n-primitive-parts)): For each positive integer $s$ there is a computable threshold $H(s)$ with the following properties for $d>H(s)$. A primitive group of degree $d$ and order at least $\lfloor\sqrt{d/s}\rfloor!/2$ has one of the alternating-product actions $$\label{n:three-actions} (e,h)=(1,1),\qquad(1,2),\qquad(2,1),$$ with $\ell$ arbitrarily large as the threshold is increased. Its socle is $A_\ell^e$ and has index at most eight. If its order is at least $\lfloor d/s\rfloor!/2$, it contains $A_d$ in the natural action. One may take $$\label{n:threshold} H(s)=2^{\,2^{(s+100)^{10}}}.$$
  - Explanation: Restricts the possible structures of high-degree primitive groups of large order to three explicit product actions of alternating groups via Maróti's theorem.
- **stmt-n-profiles** (theorem, [source](#stmt-n-profiles)): Suppose a finite set is partitioned into at most $s$ equal-sized parts $B$, each preserved by a rank-one control $X$. Write the size of $B$ as $$b_B+\sum_i k_{Bi}n_i,$$ where $b_B$ counts its fixed letters, $k_{Bi}$ counts its natural copies of the factor $A_{n_i}$ of $X$, and the number of factors and all nonnegative integers $b_B,k_{Bi}$ are at most $s$. There is a rank-one subcontrol of $X$, of complexity bounded computably in $s$, that has identical profiles on all parts. If the common part size is at least two, the subcontrol may also be chosen with at least two fixed letters in every part.
  - Explanation: Uses Dickson's Lemma and Presburger arithmetic to construct a subcontrol with equalized fixed-letter counts and natural copies across partitioned parts.
- **stmt-n-rank-one** (theorem, [source](#stmt-n-rank-one)): There are computable functions of $s$ that bound, for every rank-one control $X$ of complexity at most $s$ on a finite nonempty set $I$,* 1. *the number of transitive groups $U$ with $X\le U\le S_I$ and the index $[U:\langle X^U\rangle]$;* 2. *the length of a generating list for $U$ over $X$, chosen so that every generator $g$ has a rank-one control of computably bounded complexity inside $X\cap gXg^{-1}$.
  - Explanation: Bounds the number of transitive overgroups of rank-one controls and their relative generator lengths computably in the orbit complexity.
- **stmt-n-private-squares** (theorem, [source](#stmt-n-private-squares)): There are computable functions $B(s),C(s)$ such that every control $X$ with private squares of complexity at most $s$ on a finite nonempty set $I$ has at most $B(s)$ transitive overgroups in $S_I$, and every such overgroup $U$ satisfies $$[U:\langle X^U\rangle]\le C(s).$$ The functions can be taken nondecreasing and at least one.
  - Explanation: Extends the computable overgroup enumeration and normal closure index bounds to permutation controls containing private two-dimensional square orbits.
- **stmt-n-template-bound** (bound, [source](#stmt-n-template-bound)): There is a total computable nondecreasing function $\Phi:\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\to\mathbb Z_{\ge1}$ such that every weighted template $$F=[S_Z\times Y,S_{Z\sqcup(\bigcup T)}]$$ of [sec:weighted](#sec:weighted), with at most $t$ units, excluding the foundation $Z$ from this count, and $\|Z\|>\|\bigcup T\|$, satisfies $\|F\|\le\Phi(t)$. The bound is independent of all full-unit sizes, square sides, auxiliary axis lengths, offset sizes, and the size of $Z$. No stock-size hypothesis is required for this counting assertion.
  - Explanation: Establishes uniform computable template bound in the stated setting.
- **stmt-n-circuit-template** (theorem, [source](#stmt-n-circuit-template)): There is an absolute stock integer $S$ with the following property. For every positive circuit equation $\mathcal C$, one can compute an integer $t_S(\mathcal C)$ from its syntax such that every positive solution determines a weighted template $F$ with at most $t_S(\mathcal C)$ units. In every size reading of this template supplied by [t:weighted-realization](#t:weighted-realization), the actual raw sizes give a positive solution of $\mathcal C$ in the same cell alignment. If all cells in that reading have size at most $Q$, the resulting solution has all its value variables at most $Q$.
  - Explanation: Establishes encoding a circuit by weighted comparisons in the stated setting.
- **stmt-n-undecidable** (theorem, [source](#stmt-n-undecidable)): There is no algorithm which, given the tables of a finite lattice, decides whether it is isomorphic to the congruence lattice of a finite algebra. Equivalently, there is no total computable bound, in terms of lattice cardinality, for the minimum carrier size among all representable finite lattices.
  - Explanation: Establishes undecidability of finite representability in the stated setting.
- **stmt-n-interval-undecidable** (theorem, [source](#stmt-n-interval-undecidable)): There is no deterministic Turing machine which, given the order table of a finite nonempty lattice $L$, always halts and decides whether $L\cong[H,G]$ for some finite group $G$ and subgroup $H\le G$, where $[H,G]$ consists of every subgroup $K$ with $H\le K\le G$, ordered by inclusion. Equivalently, there is no total computable bound, in terms of lattice cardinality, on the least possible order of the top group $G$ among lattices admitting such a realization.
  - Explanation: Establishes undecidability of finite subgroup-interval recognition in the stated setting.
- **stmt-q-acf-computable** (theorem, [source](#stmt-q-acf-computable)): The integer $a(x)$ exists, is nondecreasing, and is total computable. This holds uniformly over the characteristic and the specialization of every coefficient.
  - Explanation: Establishes the stated finite representation result.
- **stmt-q-root-formats** (theorem, [source](#stmt-q-root-formats)): Let $10^9\le x\le y$ be integers, and let $G$ be split pinned, adjoint simple of rank at most $x$ over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic. Its adjoint representation embeds $G$ as a closed subgroup of $\operatorname{GL}_d$, where $d=\dim G=O((x+10)^2)$. For rational simple modules of the simply connected cover, of dimension and highest-weight coefficients at most $y$, graphs of the induced projective actions have format at most $J(y)$. Stabilizers of a subalgebra or of at most $y$ subspaces of the corresponding matrix algebra, and normalizers of projective subgroups of order at most $y$, have format at most $J^3(y)$.* *For a positive standard map of parameter $P$, the fixed-point test has a Boolean description with at most $J^5(y)$ atoms and degrees at most $J^5(y)P$. A proper closed subset of $G$ of format at most $y$ therefore contains at most $$\label{q:proper-fixed-count} J^{10}(y)P^{\dim G-1}$$ fixed points. For $P>J(y)$ the derived simple fixed group has order at least $P^{\dim G}/(10y)^4$. The same bounds apply to the other adjoint types in the stated rank range.
  - Explanation: Establishes root words and fixed points in the stated setting.
- **stmt-q-genericity** (theorem, [source](#stmt-q-genericity)): Let $x\ge10^9$, and let $G$ be adjoint simple of rank at most $x$ over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$. If a finite subgroup $\Gamma\le G$ is not contained in any proper closed subset of affine ring format at most $J^{1000}(x)$, then there is a positive-height standard point map $\Psi$ such that $$\label{q:sandwich} (G^\Psi)'\le\Gamma\le G^\Psi.$$ Proper closed subsets in this hypothesis need not be irreducible.
  - Explanation: Establishes quantitative genericity in the stated setting.
- **stmt-q-size-ceiling** (bound, [source](#stmt-q-size-ceiling)): The negative affine-chart construction has a choice of finite parameters for which its lattice $L$ is nonrepresentable and $$\|L\|<M_*.$$ In particular a nonrepresentable lattice exists among the tables of cardinality at most the ordinary computable integer $M_*$.
  - Explanation: Establishes size ceiling in the stated setting.
- **stmt-q-arithmetic-criterion** (theorem, [source](#stmt-q-arithmetic-criterion)): For every table satisfying $P(n,t)$, $$\label{q:arithmetic-R} \mathcal R\bigl((\{0,\ldots,n-1\};\preceq)\bigr) \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad (\exists j\ge1)\ Q(n,t,j).$$ Moreover $Q(n,t,j)$ holds exactly when the colored-graph criterion has a witness with $j$ vertices.
  - Explanation: Establishes that the bounded register arithmetic predicate Q(n,t,j) correctly encodes the colored-graph criterion on a carrier of size j, making finite algebra representability equivalent to the existential quantification of this arithmetic predicate.
- **stmt-q-search-size** (theorem, [source](#stmt-q-search-size)): For $1\le n\le M_*$ and $0\le t<2^{n^2}$, there is a program of [q:register-language](#q:register-language), of size less than $k$, which terminates exactly when $Q(n,t,j)$ holds for some positive $j$. On termination it outputs the least such $j$. The program contains neither $B$ nor any oracle instruction.
  - Explanation: Shows that a deterministic register program systematically tests candidate witness sizes j in increasing order without using oracles, with its syntax-tree program size strictly bounded by k.
- **stmt-q-witness-cutoff** (bound, [source](#stmt-q-witness-cutoff)): If $1\le n\le M_*$, $0\le t<2^{n^2}$, and $P(n,t)$ holds, then $$\label{q:finite-cutoff} \mathcal R(T_{n,t})\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad (\exists j\in\{1,\ldots,B\})\ Q(n,t,j).$$ In fact every representable such table has a witness of size strictly less than $B$.
  - Explanation: Proves that any representable lattice order table within the initial segment up to M_* admits a graph witness strictly smaller than the Busy Beaver bound B, converting representability on this segment into a bounded finite search.
- **stmt-q-minimum** (theorem, [source](#stmt-q-minimum)): The bounded formulas <a href="#q:selection-z" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="q:selection-z">[q:selection-z]</a>–<a href="#q:minimum-order" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="q:minimum-order">[q:minimum-order]</a>, with the ordinary unevaluated Busy Beaver constant <a href="#q:BB-bound" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="q:BB-bound">[q:BB-bound]</a>, specify the full finite order table of a nonrepresentable lattice $L_0$ of minimum cardinality. Its cardinality is the integer $a_0$ in <a href="#q:a0t0" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="q:a0t0">[q:a0t0]</a>, and $$7<a_0\le M_*.$$ This is a finite order description and a proof of minimum cardinality; it does not supply a numerically evaluated value of that cardinality.
  - Explanation: Proves that the bounded arithmetic formulas uniquely isolate the full order table of a minimal nonrepresentable lattice L_0 using an unevaluated Busy Beaver constant without requiring decimal numerical evaluation.

```json
        "anchor": "stmt-f-prop-chart-properties",
        "exact_quote": "The construction in [f:def-test-lattice](#f:def-test-lattice) gives a finite self-dual lattice $L$. It is graded of length $n+2$, atomistic, coatomistic, and simple. Any two charts intersect in a flat of each, of rank at most $m$, with the same affine structure on the intersection. Within one chart the primal join of two flats is their affine span if that span has dimension at most $n$. Attachment preserves all old meets and joins. In particular, flats in two distinct private charts attached at the same $W$, neither contained in $W$, have no common proper primal upper bound. There are at least three horizontal comparability components in the interior of $L$, each containing a chain of distinct comparable interior elements.",
        "source_id": "PM-206.1"

        "exact_quote": "<span id=\"f:prop-prepared-links\" label=\"f:prop-prepared-links\"></span> If $X$ is a nonempty flat of rank at most $m$ in a trunk chart, the reverse ideal with top $X$, denoted $[0,X]$, is graded, atomistic, and coatomistic. The following additional properties hold for $L$ and for every such prepared link.*\n\n1.  *<span id=\"f:link-diamonds\" label=\"f:link-diamonds\"></span> Every bottom interval of length two is a diamond $M_b$ with $b\\ge3$ atoms, where $b-1\\ge2$ is not a prime power.*\n\n2.  *<span id=\"f:link-upper-diamonds\" label=\"f:link-upper-diamonds\"></span> In every interior component there is an element $y$ two ranks below the interval’s top whose upper interval is a diamond with at least two middle elements.*\n\n*In addition, $L$ has the following separation property:*\n\n1.  *For any atom $u$ and any proper upper bound $\\omega\\ge u$, there is a rank-two element $z\\ge u$ with $z\\not\\le\\omega$.",

        "anchor": "stmt-f-lem-subdirect",
        "exact_quote": "A subdirect subgroup of a finite power of a nonabelian simple group is a product of full, possibly automorphism-twisted, diagonal subgroups on disjoint parts partitioning the coordinates. Containment between two such subgroups means refinement of the tied parts, with agreement of the diagonal identifications on each refined part. If a subgroup contains the untwisted full diagonal, all its diagonal identifications are untwisted.",

        "anchor": "stmt-f-prop-monolith",
        "exact_quote": "Suppose $[H,G]$ is isomorphic either to $L$ or to a prepared reverse link.         "anchor": "stmt-f-lem-extension-description",
        "exact_quote": "Suppose $H$ acts by automorphisms on $S^s$, transitively on the simple coordinates. Fix a coordinate $o$, identify its group with $S$, and let $A_0\\le H$ be its stabilizer, with induced action $\\alpha:A_0\\to\\operatorname{Aut}(S)$.         "exact_quote": "Fix an extension datum as in [f:def-pure-extension](#f:def-pure-extension), and an affine four-space over a finite field with at least three elements.         "exact_quote": "Suppose $H\\le K\\le K_W$, and a local conclusion in $K_W/C_W$ supplies a nonabelian simple normal subgroup $\\overline B\\trianglelefteq K/C_W$ contained in the image of $B_W$. Suppose also that $(H/C_W)\\overline B=K/C_W$, and that its centralizer in $K/C_W$ is soluble and contained in $H/C_W$. Then $\\overline B$ has a unique lift $B\\le B_W$, with $$B\\trianglelefteq K,\\qquad HB=K,\\qquad C_K(B)\\le H,$$ and $C_K(B)$ is soluble. The quotient by this centralizer is almost simple. If the earlier actual socles contain $B_W$, the image of $B$ in every earlier ancestor quotient agrees with any nonabelian simple normal subgroup supplied there with soluble centralizer.       "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-w-lp",
        "exact_quote": "For the fixed finite list of simple adjoint types, there is a uniform degree bound $d_0$ with the following property.         "exact_quote": "Let $S_i$ be a high classical ancestor, and let $B$ be a candidate simple subgroup of high classical type in the same defining characteristic.         "anchor": "stmt-w-rational-composition",
        "exact_quote": "Let $i<j<l$ lie in one protected run, and suppose these three nodes have the same series A, B, C, or D.       "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-w-universal-cuts",
        "exact_quote": "Use the triple, groups, and weights of [w:rational-composition](#w:rational-composition). Let $\\Omega$ be the full weight multiset of $L_J(\\eta)$, with every multiplicity retained. After mapping a maximal torus of $J$ into one of $G_s$, the natural weights restrict to $p^y\\Omega$. One Weyl translate of $\\lambda$ maximizes throughout the positive cocharacter chamber of $J$, and on each active fundamental summand of $\\lambda$.*\n\n*In type A an active node $a$ of the upper weight $\\lambda$ therefore gives a cut selecting $a$ entries of $\\Omega$, each dominating every unselected entry, with no equal-vector tie across the cut. In B and C the analogous signed fundamental cut selects $a$ entries, including the last node up to the B spin scale; its selected weights are nonzero and in the positive cone. This also holds at the nonspin D nodes when $\\lambda$ has no spin support. At an active D spin node the maximum instead chooses one orientation $u_a$ of each natural signed pair, and $$u_a+u_b\\text{ is nonnegative on the chamber whenever }a\\ne b.$$ Distinct ambient orbit weights cannot restrict to the same highest weight. More generally, every weight of a simple highest module differing from highest by a multiple of one simple root has multiplicity at most one.",
        "source_id": "PM-206.1"
      },
      "evidence": [
        {
          "anchor": "stmt-w-universal-cuts",
          "exact_quote": "Use the triple, groups, and weights of [w:rational-composition](#w:rational-composition). One Weyl translate of $\\lambda$ maximizes throughout the positive cocharacter chamber of $J$, and on each active fundamental summand of $\\lambda$.*\n\n*In type A an active node $a$ of the upper weight $\\lambda$ therefore gives a cut selecting $a$ entries of $\\Omega$, each dominating every unselected entry, with no equal-vector tie across the cut. In B and C the analogous signed fundamental cut selects $a$ entries, including the last node up to the B spin scale; its selected weights are nonzero and in the positive cone. This also holds at the nonspin D nodes when $\\lambda$ has no spin support. At an active D spin node the maximum instead chooses one orientation $u_a$ of each natural signed pair, and $$u_a+u_b\\text{ is nonnegative on the chamber whenever }a\\ne b.$$ Distinct ambient orbit weights cannot restrict to the same highest weight. They are closed under meets and joins in the original interval. Write $K_X$ for the ordinary label indexed by a prime-generated $X\\le A_n$. For every bounded-size semiregular elementary $q$-group $X$, including $1$, with $q>5$ prime, the interval $[H,K_X]$ has property $(*)$, has base equal to a meet of strictly intermediate coatoms, and has arbitrarily large residual height when $n/|X|$ is sufficiently large. These conclusions persist under the core and centralizer quotients whose kernels lie in the base.",

        "anchor": "stmt-r-projective-charts",
        "exact_quote": "Fix a prime $q>5$, a bounded path depth $D$, a maximum increment $r$, and finite chart dimensions and numbers. At a node $W$, each private chart is $W\\oplus\\mathbf F_q^N$ and extends the prescribed action of $W$.         "anchor": "stmt-fa-projector-maximal",
        "exact_quote": "Let $V=W\\oplus U$, with $0<\\dim U<\\dim W$, be a nondegenerate splitting in an isometry type, or an image–kernel splitting in linear type with anti-actions. Let $M$ be a group of the corresponding classical actions containing the natural special group, and let $K$ be the full ordered splitting stabilizer, equivalently the idempotent stabilizer for the ring action. Assume that $K$ supplements the special group in $M$, that its collineations act semilinearly irreducibly on $U$, and that the supported special group on $W$ is available, as is that on $U$ when $\\dim U$ is large. In the linear case assume also that $K$ contains an anti-action fixing the projector, hence carrying its image–kernel data into the dual annihilator data.         "anchor": "stmt-fa-degree-gap",
        "exact_quote": "For a sufficiently high-rank classical simple group of natural dimension $m$, with the type and characteristic conventions of [w:classical-conventions](#w:classical-conventions), a nontrivial irreducible projective representation in defining characteristic has degree at least $m$. Unless it is natural up to Frobenius and duality, its degree is at least $$\\frac{m^2}{2}-O(m).$$ A highest weight with $l$ nonzero digit places has degree at least $m^l$. For field parameter $P$, every nontrivial cross-characteristic projective representation has degree at least $P^{cm}$, for an absolute $c>0$; the same exponential lower bound holds for permutation degree. These lower bounds on nontrivial contributions apply to perfect central lifts and quotients. Finally, a high-degree alternating simple group acting projectively nontrivially in dimension $v$ has natural alternating degree $O(v)$.",

An ordinary realization of a nontrivial weighted image, in either orientation and with top order $M$, gives a forward realization after at most that many marker deletions, with all cuts product in an actual alternating power. A single common cell alignment gives positive sizes $u_j\\le M$, equal on each cohort and one on all surviving markers. In this same alignment the equal-total reading of [t:weighted-equal-totals](#t:weighted-equal-totals) and the square reading of [t:weighted-square](#t:weighted-square) hold.*\n\n*If the input is a finite algebra of size $m$ representing a nontrivial image, the same conclusion holds with $M=60^m m!$, for a possibly different nontrivial image of the original template. The full template itself is finitely representable.",
          "source_id": "PM-206.1"
        }

      "quantifiers": [

          "anchor": "stmt-n-circuit-template",
          "exact_quote": "There is an absolute stock integer $S$ with the following property. For every positive circuit equation $\\mathcal C$, one can compute an integer $t_S(\\mathcal C)$ from its syntax such that every positive solution determines a weighted template $F$ with at most $t_S(\\mathcal C)$ units. In every size reading of this template supplied by [t:weighted-realization](#t:weighted-realization), the actual raw sizes give a positive solution of $\\mathcal C$ in the same cell alignment. If all cells in that reading have size at most $Q$, the resulting solution has all its value variables at most $Q$.",
```

<a id="pm-s2"></a>
## 2. Definitions, validity and bounds

- **Admissible placements** ([source](#stmt-f-def-placement)): An $L$-colored complete graph consists of a finite nonempty vertex set $A$ and a symmetric function $d:A\times A\to L$, with $d(p,p)=0$. Loops are included among its edges. A placement into another such graph $(A',d')$ is a map $f:A\to A'$; it is *admissible* if $$d'(f(p),f(q))\le d(p,q)\qquad(p,q\in A).$$ For a nonempty set $S$ of edges of $(A,d)$, let $\Gamma_S$ be the undirected graph on $A$ whose marked adjacencies are the pairs $\{f(p),f(q)\}$, where $\{p,q\}\in S$ and $f:A\to A$ is admissible. Collapsed pairs are allowed and do not affect connectivity. Write $a_S=\bigvee_{\{p,q\}\in S}d(p,q)$.
- **The exceptional small lattice** ([source](#stmt-f-def-l7)): Let $L_7$ have elements $0,1,a,b,c,d,x$, with $0$ least, $1$ greatest, and with the comparabilities among the five interior elements exactly $$a<c,\qquad b<c,\qquad b<d.$$ In DeMeo’s group-interval labeling these elements are $J_1,J_2,M_2,M_1,K$, respectively.
- **Affine test lattice** ([source](#stmt-f-def-test-lattice)): Let $q\ge5$ be a prime power such that $q-1$ is not a prime power, and let $r,D,g,m,n,N$ be positive integers satisfying $$\label{f:eq-parameters} D\ge2,\qquad g\ge2,\qquad 3\le m<n-2,\qquad Dr<m,\qquad N\ge n+2.$$ There are arbitrarily large allowable $q$, for example powers of $7$. A *chart* is a copy of $\operatorname{AG}(N,q)$. The rank of a nonempty affine flat is its affine dimension plus one; the empty flat has rank zero. To attach a fresh chart at a specified flat $W$, identify a flat of the new chart affinely with $W$, and take all its other points fresh. Its intersection with the union of the old point sets is exactly $W$. Attachment at the empty flat makes no identifications. Build the trunk charts recursively, beginning with the path ending at $W=\varnothing$. 1. At a path ending at $W$, attach $g$ fresh *private charts* at $W$. 2. In each such chart, reserve a child path extending this path by $U$ for every flat $U\supset W$ with rank increment between $1$ and $r$. Perform stages for $D$ generations: the empty path has a stage, as does every child path reached in fewer than $D$ steps. 3. Finally, at every nonempty flat of rank at most $m$ in a trunk chart, attach at least one additional fresh *leaf chart*, with no stages of its own. Repeated reservations may use distinct fresh charts. There are only finitely many charts. The primal interior labels are the point sets that are nonempty affine flats of dimension at most $n$ in some chart, ordered by inclusion. Adjoin the empty bottom and one formal top above all these labels, obtaining a bounded poset $L^+$. Let $L^-$ be an order-reversed copy of $L^+$. The *test lattice* $L$ is their horizontal sum: identify the two bottoms and the two tops, with no other cross-comparabilities. The interior labels on $L^-$ are called *reverse flats*, named by their affine point sets; their lattice order reverses inclusion. On this side the top may accordingly be called the empty flat.
- **Extension data and purity** ([source](#stmt-f-def-pure-extension)): An extension datum consists of a subgroup $H$ of a finite ambient group $K$, a nonabelian simple group $B$, and a homomorphism $\psi:H\to\operatorname{Aut}(B)$ whose image contains $B$, identified with its inner automorphisms. Its extension poset consists of all homomorphisms $\beta:T\to\operatorname{Aut}(B)$, $H\le T\le K$, restricting to $\psi$, ordered by extension, together with an artificial top. Put $$D_0=\ker\psi,\qquad P_0=\psi^{-1}(B).$$ An extension is *pure* if $\beta(T)=\psi(H)$, equivalently $T=H\ker\beta$.
- **Bounded equation complexity** ([source](#stmt-w-complexity)): Fix closed affine split models for the root systems in the finite list, with a bounded number of coordinates and bounded-degree group operations. A closed subset has equation complexity at most $d$ if it is the common zero set, inside the chosen group, of polynomials of degree at most $d$. There need not be a previously specified bound on the number of equations: their linear span lies in the finite-dimensional space of polynomials of degree at most $d$.
- **Prepared paths and ancestor properties** ([source](#stmt-w-prepared-path)): A *prepared path* is a strict descending chain of finite groups $K_W$ containing a common subgroup $H$, together with actual strictly nested nonabelian simple groups $B_W\trianglelefteq K_W$ such that $$HB_W=K_W,\qquad C_{K_W}(B_W)\le H,$$ where each centralizer is soluble and the quotient by it is almost simple with socle $B_W$. Fix the usual natural realizations of the alternating and classical socles. For every ancestor–descendant pair require the following properties. 1. In an alternating ancestor, the descendant socle is transitive on the natural set. 2. In a high classical ancestor, the descendant socle is projectively absolutely irreducible on the natural module. Its label normalizes no proper ground-field tensor system of the endomorphism algebra of the kind excluded in [sec:classical](#sec:classical); in isometry types the factors are individually selfadjoint.
- **A protected classical run** ([source](#stmt-w-protected)): A consecutive high classical run of one defining characteristic is *protected* if for every ancestor–descendant pair within the run the descendant has one tensor atom on the ancestor natural module and no prime root of the ancestor Steinberg map fixes it pointwise. The path also retains all properties of [w:prepared-path](#w:prepared-path).
- **Pure marker lattice** ([source](#stmt-r-pure-markers)): For a finite set $T$ of $t$ markers, let $F_T$ have labels $$(I,V),\qquad I\subseteq T,\quad V\le S_{T\setminus I}.$$ Choose a set $Z$ disjoint from $T$, with $\|Z\|=t+1$ or larger, and interpret this label as the subgroup $$S_{Z\cup I}\times V\ \le S_{Z\cup T}.$$ Order, meet, and join are subgroup containment, intersection, and generation in this model. The markers in $I$ are called absorbed. We write $$X_I=(I,1),\qquad x_i=X_{\{i\}},\qquad M_D=X_{T\setminus D},\qquad C_D=(T\setminus D,S_D)\quad(D\ne\varnothing).$$ The bottom and top are $X_\varnothing$ and $X_T$. We also write $F_t$ when only the cardinality matters.
- **Units and stock** ([source](#stmt-t-weighted-units)): We use disjoint transitive permutation sets called units; their index set is denoted by $T$, and symmetric-group notation on a set of indices (when talking about permutations of letters) uses the entire union of their units. There are singleton markers. On the units we take independent groups with product $Y$, of these kinds: - full symmetric groups, including on the markers; - primary squares of side $x$, with group $A_x\times A_x$ slotwise, where $8\mid x,\ x\ge16$; - auxiliary units of shape $(x/4)\times2\times2$ (same side-parameter restrictions), with *full symmetric groups slotwise*. For each primary side there is its auxiliary type (total size $x$), and for each axis length used there are full reference units of that size. Units are supplied in cohorts of identical type and size. Also, for each non-marker cohort so required (or basic extra full cohort used), include a full offset cohort of size per unit one greater than its total size per unit. These extra offsets themselves need no new offsets. In what follows every cohort, including markers, can be required to have at least a sufficiently large number of members. For the group-structural tests this lower bound can be *absolute*, independent of sizes and number of cohorts. We explain the finite losses involved along with the arguments. Assume there are nonmarker units in this use.
- **Weighted template** ([source](#stmt-t-weighted-template)): Adjoin a foundation set $Z$ larger than all the letters together. Use the ordinary interval $$F=[S_Z\times Y,S_{Z\sqcup(\cup T)}].$$ (Here $\cup T$ denotes the union of the units.) The notation for its labels is $$(I,U)=S_{Z\sqcup(\cup I)}\times U,\qquad I\subseteq T,\quad Y_{T\setminus I}\le U\le S_{T\setminus I}.$$ The set $I$ is the *footprint*: its units have been absorbed into the foundation orbit.
- **Product success** ([source](#stmt-t-weighted-success-definition)): We say that *product success* holds when a forward realization in a nonabelian simple power has nontrivial projections of its base intersection at every site and every cut coatom is a product subgroup. We allow passage to this configuration by deleting one marker in an axis filter.
- **Controls** ([source](#stmt-n-controls)): A *rank-one control* on a finite set $I$ is a group $X$ that is a product of independent alternating groups $A_{n_i}$, with $n_i\ge7$. Each factor acts naturally on one or more disjoint copies of its alphabet, using the same permutation on all its copies, and fixes all other letters. Additional fixed letters are allowed, as is the trivial group. Its *complexity* is the number of its orbits on $I$. A *control with private squares* is the disjoint combination of a rank-one control and square orbits, each with its own two independent natural alternating factors. The factors of a square act on no other orbit. The two alphabets of each square have the same size, at least seven. Its complexity again counts all orbits, including fixed letters. A *trimmed control* fixes a specified bounded number of entries in each alphabet and retains the alternating action on the remaining entries. If fewer than seven entries remain, the whole remaining alphabet is declared fixed.
- **Positive circuits** ([source](#stmt-n-positive-circuits)): A positive circuit is a finite arithmetic circuit with positive integer input variables, constant $1$, and addition and multiplication gates. A *value variable* records either an input or a gate value. A circuit equation requires equality of two designated outputs.
- **Affine ring format** ([source](#stmt-q-format)): For an integer $x\ge10^9$, an affine ring formula has *format at most $x$* if it has at most $x$ occurrences in total of polynomial-equality atoms and the operations $\neg,\land,\lor,\exists,\forall$, at most $x$ variables, and polynomial atoms of total degree at most $x$. Occurrences are counted in the formula tree, with a separate variable for each quantifier binder. The variable count includes the entire ambient affine coordinate list, even unused coordinates. Coefficients are arbitrary field elements, and a polynomial is counted through its atom and degree, rather than its expanded arithmetic expression. Let $a(x)$ be the least positive simultaneous bound, over all algebraically closed fields and formulas of format at most $x$, for both the format of an equivalent quantifier-free formula in the same ambient coordinates and the number and degrees of polynomial equations defining its Zariski closure.
- **The function $J$** ([source](#stmt-q-j)): Let $R(c,h)$ be the least positive set size forcing a monochromatic $h$-element subset in every $c$-coloring of its unordered pairs of distinct elements. Let $\operatorname{HJ}(a,c,s)$ be the least positive word length forcing a monochromatic $s$-slot word family over an $a$-letter alphabet in every $c$-coloring. Here some positions have fixed letters, possibly no positions do, and the others are partitioned into $s$ disjoint nonempty sets; each set carries one independently arbitrary common letter. Put $$\begin{aligned} J(x)=1+\max\bigl(&\{2^{2^{x!}},a(x)\} \cup\{R(c,h):1\le c,h\le x\}\notag\\ &\cup\{\operatorname{HJ}(a,c,s):1\le a,c,s\le x\}\bigr). \label{q:J-formula} \end{aligned}$$ The notation $J^d$ denotes iteration, not an ordinary power.
- **The computable ceiling sequence** ([source](#stmt-q-ceiling-sequence)): Set $$\label{q:x-sequence} x_0=10^9,\qquad x_{j+1}=J^{x_j}(x_j)\quad(0\le j<5), \qquad M_*=x_5.$$ These are ordinary computable integers.
- **Register programs and size** ([source](#stmt-q-register-language)): Registers $v_i$, $i\ge0$, hold natural numbers and initially all contain zero. Terms use these registers, the constants $0,1$, addition, truncated subtraction $u\mathbin{\dot-}v$, multiplication, exponentiation $u^v$, and integer floor quotient. We set $0^0=1$ and give quotient by zero the value zero. Bounded formulas use the binary predicates $=,<$, the connectives $\neg,\land,\lor$, and quantifiers $\exists v_i<t$, $\forall v_i<t$, with $v_i$ absent from the bound term $t$. A variable bound within a formula is local to that formula and does not write to a register. Programs are formed by assignments of terms to registers, binary sequencing, if-then-else with a bounded condition and two program branches, and while with a bounded condition and a program body. They have the usual deterministic semantics. A terminating program outputs its final value of $v_0$. The size of a program is its syntax-tree cost: each operation, constant, predicate, connective, quantifier, assignment, sequencing, if-then-else, or while node costs one. Each occurrence of $v_i$ costs $1+i$, including assignment targets and quantifier binders. Parentheses cost nothing, and no extra cost is charged for the use of a quantifier’s term as its bound.
- **The Busy Beaver cutoff** ([source](#stmt-q-bb)): With $M_*=x_5$ as in <a href="#q:x-sequence" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="q:x-sequence">[q:x-sequence]</a>, set $$\label{q:BB-bound} \begin{split} k&=2^{(M_*+10)^4},\\ B&=1+\max\Bigl(\{0\}\cup \{\operatorname{output}(p):p\text{ terminates and has size } \le k\}\Bigr). \end{split}$$ The programs in this definition use exactly [q:register-language](#q:register-language); in particular $B$ is not a symbol in their language.
- **Digits and order tables** ([source](#stmt-q-table-predicate)): For $b\ge1$, put $$\label{q:digit} \operatorname{dig}_b(z,i)= \left\lfloor\frac{z}{b^i}\right\rfloor \mathbin{\dot-} b\left\lfloor\frac{z}{b^{i+1}}\right\rfloor.$$ Base $1$ is used only where the intended digit is zero, in which case this formula indeed gives zero. For $n\ge1$ and $0\le t<2^{n^2}$, let $T_{n,t}$ be the relation on $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ defined by $$\label{q:order-bit} a\preceq b\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \operatorname{dig}_2(t,an+b)=1.$$ Write $E(a,b)$ for the right side, with $n,t$ understood. The bounded predicate $P(n,t)$ says that $T_{n,t}$ is a lattice: it is the conjunction of $$\begin{aligned} &\forall a<n\ E(a,a),\\ &\forall a,b<n\ \bigl((E(a,b)\land E(b,a))\Longrightarrow a=b\bigr),\\ &\forall a,b,c<n\ \bigl((E(a,b)\land E(b,c))\Longrightarrow E(a,c)\bigr), \end{aligned}$$ and the following two assertions for every $a,b<n$: $$\begin{aligned} \exists u<n\ \bigl(&E(a,u)\land E(b,u)\land \forall v<n\,((E(a,v)\land E(b,v))\Longrightarrow E(u,v))\bigr),\\ \exists l<n\ \bigl(&E(l,a)\land E(l,b)\land \forall v<n\,((E(v,a)\land E(v,b))\Longrightarrow E(v,l))\bigr). \end{aligned}$$ Repeated bounded variables denote successive quantifiers with the displayed bound. Implication, equivalence, and non-strict comparison throughout this section abbreviate their expressions using the primitive connectives and $=,<$.
- **The witness predicate** ([source](#stmt-q-witness-predicate)): For $j\ge1$, the formula $Q(n,t,j)$ asserts that there is $$\label{q:color-encoding} z<n^{j^2},\qquad d(p,q)=\operatorname{dig}_n(z,pj+q)\quad(p,q<j),$$ with the following properties. First, the colors are symmetric, bottom occurs exactly on loops, and the triangle inequality holds. Explicitly, set $\operatorname{Bot}(a)\equiv\forall b<n\ E(a,b)$ and require $$\begin{aligned} &\forall p,q<j\quad d(p,q)=d(q,p),\notag\\ &\forall p,q<j\quad \bigl(\operatorname{Bot}(d(p,q))\longleftrightarrow p=q\bigr), \label{q:graph-bottom}\\ &\forall p,q,u<j\ \forall b<n\quad \bigl(E(d(p,u),b)\land E(d(u,q),b)\bigr) \Longrightarrow E(d(p,q),b).\notag \end{aligned}$$ Second, require order reflection: $$\label{q:graph-reflect} \forall a,b<n\quad \neg E(a,b)\Longrightarrow \exists p,q<j\ \bigl(E(d(p,q),a)\land\neg E(d(p,q),b)\bigr).$$ For the third requirement, let $0<s<2^{j^2}$ be a nonempty ordered-pair mask and write $\operatorname{Sel}_s(p,q)\equiv\operatorname{dig}_2(s,pj+q)=1$. A number $f<j^j$ specifies a vertex map by $f[p]=\operatorname{dig}_j(f,p)$. Set $$\label{q:placement-arithmetic} \operatorname{Adm}(f)\equiv \forall p,q<j\ E\bigl(d(f[p],f[q]),d(p,q)\bigr).$$ The derived undirected adjacency is the bounded predicate $$\label{q:adjacency-arithmetic} \begin{split} \operatorname{Adj}_s(r,r')\equiv\exists f<j^j\ \bigl( &\operatorname{Adm}(f)\land \exists a,b<j\ \bigl(\operatorname{Sel}_s(a,b)\land\\[-2pt] &((f[a]=r\land f[b]=r')\lor (f[a]=r'\land f[b]=r))\bigr)\bigr). \end{split}$$ For $h<j^{j+1}$, put $h[i]=\operatorname{dig}_j(h,i)$, and define $$\label{q:path-arithmetic} \begin{split} \operatorname{Path}_s(p,q)\equiv\exists h<j^{j+1}\ \bigl( &h[0]=p\land h[j]=q\land\\[-2pt] &\forall i<j\ (h[i]=h[i+1]\lor \operatorname{Adj}_s(h[i],h[i+1]))\bigr). \end{split}$$ Write $$\begin{aligned} \operatorname{Up}_s(b)&\equiv \forall a,c<j\, \bigl(\operatorname{Sel}_s(a,c)\Longrightarrow E(d(a,c),b)\bigr), \label{q:mask-upper}\\ \operatorname{BelowJoin}_s(p,q)&\equiv \forall b<n\, \bigl(\operatorname{Up}_s(b)\Longrightarrow E(d(p,q),b)\bigr). \notag \end{aligned}$$ The third requirement is $$\label{q:graph-connect-arithmetic} \forall s<2^{j^2}\quad s\ne0\Longrightarrow \forall p,q<j\, \bigl(\operatorname{BelowJoin}_s(p,q) \Longrightarrow\operatorname{Path}_s(p,q)\bigr).$$ The conjunction of all three initial color requirements—symmetry, the bottom condition <a href="#q:graph-bottom" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="q:graph-bottom">[q:graph-bottom]</a>, and the triangle condition— with <a href="#q:graph-reflect" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="q:graph-reflect">[q:graph-reflect]</a> and <a href="#q:graph-connect-arithmetic" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="q:graph-connect-arithmetic">[q:graph-connect-arithmetic]</a>, under the existential quantifier in <a href="#q:color-encoding" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="q:color-encoding">[q:color-encoding]</a>, is $Q(n,t,j)$.
- **Carrier and order** ([source](#stmt-q-minimum-table)): Let $$\mathcal I=\{(n,t):1\le n\le M_*,\ 0\le t<2^{n^2}\}$$ have increasing pair-lexicographic order, with $n$ compared first. Define $$\label{q:selection-z} z_{n,t}=\begin{cases} 1,& P(n,t)\ \text{and}\ (\forall j=1,\ldots,B)\ \neg Q(n,t,j),\\ 0,&\text{otherwise}, \end{cases}$$ and, with the empty product equal to one, $$\label{q:selection-w} w_{n,t}=z_{n,t} \prod_{\substack{(m,u)\in\mathcal I\\(m,u)<(n,t)}} (1-z_{m,u}).$$ Set $$\label{q:a0t0} a_0=\sum_{(n,t)\in\mathcal I}n w_{n,t},\qquad t_0=\sum_{(n,t)\in\mathcal I}t w_{n,t}.$$ The structure $L_0$ has carrier $\{i:0\le i<a_0\}$ and order $$\label{q:minimum-order} i\le_{L_0}l\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \operatorname{dig}_2(t_0,ia_0+l)=1.$$
- **Finite algebra** ([source](#pm-h-3)): A finite algebra means a nonempty finite set $A$, together with a finite list of total operations of finite nonnegative arity.
- **Full subgroup interval** ([source](#pm-h-5)): A subgroup interval $[H,G]$ always means the whole interval.

```json
          "exact_quote": "Let $q\\ge5$ be a prime power such that $q-1$ is not a prime power, and let $r,D,g,m,n,N$ be positive integers satisfying $$\\label{f:eq-parameters}\n D\\ge2,\\qquad g\\ge2,\\qquad 3\\le m<n-2,\\qquad Dr<m,\\qquad N\\ge n+2.$$ There are arbitrarily large allowable $q$, for example powers of $7$. A *chart* is a copy of $\\operatorname{AG}(N,q)$. The rank of a nonempty affine flat is its affine dimension plus one; the empty flat has rank zero. To attach a fresh chart at a specified flat $W$, identify a flat of the new chart affinely with $W$, and take all its other points fresh. Its intersection with the union of the old point sets is exactly $W$. Attachment at the empty flat makes no identifications.\n\nBuild the trunk charts recursively, beginning with the path ending at $W=\\varnothing$.\n\n1.  At a path ending at $W$, attach $g$ fresh *private charts* at $W$.\n\n2.  In each such chart, reserve a child path extending this path by $U$ for every flat $U\\supset W$ with rank increment between $1$ and $r$. Perform stages for $D$ generations: the empty path has a stage, as does every child path reached in fewer than $D$ steps.\n\n3.  Finally, at every nonempty flat of rank at most $m$ in a trunk chart, attach at least one additional fresh *leaf chart*, with no stages of its own.\n\nRepeated reservations may use distinct fresh charts. There are only finitely many charts. The primal interior labels are the point sets that are nonempty affine flats of dimension at most $n$ in some chart, ordered by inclusion. Adjoin the empty bottom and one formal top above all these labels, obtaining a bounded poset $L^+$. Let $L^-$ be an order-reversed copy of $L^+$. The *test lattice* $L$ is their horizontal sum: identify the two bottoms and the two tops, with no other cross-comparabilities. The interior labels on $L^-$ are called *reverse flats*, named by their affine point sets; their lattice order reverses inclusion. On this side the top may accordingly be called the empty flat.",

          "anchor": "stmt-n-controls",
          "exact_quote": "A *rank-one control* on a finite set $I$ is a group $X$ that is a product of independent alternating groups $A_{n_i}$, with $n_i\\ge7$. Each factor acts naturally on one or more disjoint copies of its alphabet, using the same permutation on all its copies, and fixes all other letters. Additional fixed letters are allowed, as is the trivial group. Its *complexity* is the number of its orbits on $I$.\n\nA *control with private squares* is the disjoint combination of a rank-one control and square orbits, each with its own two independent natural alternating factors. The factors of a square act on no other orbit. The two alphabets of each square have the same size, at least seven. Its complexity again counts all orbits, including fixed letters.\n\nA *trimmed control* fixes a specified bounded number of entries in each alphabet and retains the alternating action on the remaining entries.           "anchor": "stmt-q-j",
          "exact_quote": "Let $R(c,h)$ be the least positive set size forcing a monochromatic $h$-element subset in every $c$-coloring of its unordered pairs of distinct elements.           "anchor": "stmt-q-register-language",
          "exact_quote": "Registers $v_i$, $i\\ge0$, hold natural numbers and initially all contain zero. Terms use these registers, the constants $0,1$, addition, truncated subtraction $u\\mathbin{\\dot-}v$, multiplication, exponentiation $u^v$, and integer floor quotient. We set $0^0=1$ and give quotient by zero the value zero. Bounded formulas use the binary predicates $=,<$, the connectives $\\neg,\\land,\\lor$, and quantifiers $\\exists v_i<t$, $\\forall v_i<t$, with $v_i$ absent from the bound term $t$. A variable bound within a formula is local to that formula and does not write to a register.\n\nPrograms are formed by assignments of terms to registers, binary sequencing, if-then-else with a bounded condition and two program branches, and while with a bounded condition and a program body. They have the usual deterministic semantics. A terminating program outputs its final value of $v_0$.\n\nThe size of a program is its syntax-tree cost: each operation, constant, predicate, connective, quantifier, assignment, sequencing, if-then-else, or while node costs one. Each occurrence of $v_i$ costs $1+i$, including assignment targets and quantifier binders. Parentheses cost nothing, and no extra cost is charged for the use of a quantifier’s term as its bound.",

        }

          "exact_quote": "For $j\\ge1$, the formula $Q(n,t,j)$ asserts that there is $$\\label{q:color-encoding}\n z<n^{j^2},\\qquad d(p,q)=\\operatorname{dig}_n(z,pj+q)\\quad(p,q<j),$$ with the following properties.\n\n\n\nFirst, the colors are symmetric, bottom occurs exactly on loops, and the triangle inequality holds. Explicitly, set $\\operatorname{Bot}(a)\\equiv\\forall b<n\\ E(a,b)$ and require $$\\begin{aligned}\n &\\forall p,q<j\\quad d(p,q)=d(q,p),\\notag\\\\\n &\\forall p,q<j\\quad\n        \\bigl(\\operatorname{Bot}(d(p,q))\\longleftrightarrow p=q\\bigr),\n        \\label{q:graph-bottom}\\\\\n &\\forall p,q,u<j\\ \\forall b<n\\quad\n \\bigl(E(d(p,u),b)\\land E(d(u,q),b)\\bigr)\n                       \\Longrightarrow E(d(p,q),b).\\notag\n\\end{aligned}$$ Second, require order reflection: $$\\label{q:graph-reflect}\n \\forall a,b<n\\quad \\neg E(a,b)\\Longrightarrow\n  \\exists p,q<j\\ \\bigl(E(d(p,q),a)\\land\\neg E(d(p,q),b)\\bigr).$$\n\n\nFor the third requirement, let $0<s<2^{j^2}$ be a nonempty ordered-pair mask and write $\\operatorname{Sel}_s(p,q)\\equiv\\operatorname{dig}_2(s,pj+q)=1$. A number $f<j^j$ specifies a vertex map by $f[p]=\\operatorname{dig}_j(f,p)$. Set $$\\label{q:placement-arithmetic}\n \\operatorname{Adm}(f)\\equiv\n   \\forall p,q<j\\ E\\bigl(d(f[p],f[q]),d(p,q)\\bigr).$$ The derived undirected adjacency is the bounded predicate $$\\label{q:adjacency-arithmetic}\n \\begin{split}\n \\operatorname{Adj}_s(r,r')\\equiv\\exists f<j^j\\ \\bigl(\n   &\\operatorname{Adm}(f)\\land\n       \\exists a,b<j\\ \\bigl(\\operatorname{Sel}_s(a,b)\\land\\\\[-2pt]\n   &((f[a]=r\\land f[b]=r')\\lor\n                     (f[a]=r'\\land f[b]=r))\\bigr)\\bigr).\n \\end{split}$$ For $h<j^{j+1}$, put h[j]=q\\land\\\\[-2pt]\n      &\\forall i<j\\ (h[i]=h[i+1]\\lor\n                            \\operatorname{Adj}_s(h[i],h[i+1]))\\bigr).\n \\end{split}$$ Write $$\\begin{aligned}\n \\Longrightarrow\\operatorname{Path}_s(p,q)\\bigr).$$ The conjunction of all three initial color requirements—symmetry, the bottom condition <a href=\"#q:graph-bottom\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\"           "exact_quote": "Let $$\\mathcal I=\\{(n,t):1\\le n\\le M_*,\\ 0\\le t<2^{n^2}\\}$$ have increasing pair-lexicographic order, with $n$ compared first. ## 3. Proof roadmap
```

- **f-graph-connectivity** [claim](#stmt-f-graph-connectivity) / [proof](#proof-stmt-f-graph-connectivity): Enumerate finite colorings and admissible selfmaps, then test path connectivity. -> A finite witness criterion
- **f-cor-witness-bound** [claim](#stmt-f-cor-witness-bound) / [proof](#proof-stmt-f-cor-witness-bound): Enumerate graph witnesses and compare bounded search with a hypothetical decider. -> Positive semidecidability and the witness-bound equivalence
- **f-small-lattices** [claim](#stmt-f-small-lattices) / [proof](#proof-stmt-f-small-lattices): Use the exceptional subgroup interval and the coset-action correspondence with the small-lattice reduction. -> Representability throughout the stated small-cardinality range
- **f-thm-almost-simple-reduction** [claim](#stmt-f-thm-almost-simple-reduction) / [proof](#proof-stmt-f-thm-almost-simple-reduction): Eliminate extension-kernel data using the affine grid obstruction. -> An ordinary almost simple starting interval
- **w-path-bound** [claim](#stmt-w-path-bound) / [proof](#proof-stmt-w-path-bound): Combine simultaneous protections, weight cuts, multiplicity obstructions and finite Ramsey theory. -> An absolute obstruction to long prepared paths
- **f-negative-family** [claim](#stmt-f-negative-family) / [proof](#proof-stmt-w-path-bound-2): Choose enough affine generations to contradict the protected path bound. -> A nonrepresentable finite family
- **t-weighted-realization** [claim](#stmt-t-weighted-realization) / [proof](#proof-stmt-t-weighted-realization): Transfer arbitrary realizations to alternating powers and recover all cell readings in one alignment. -> Simultaneous equal-total and square readings
- **n-template-bound** [claim](#stmt-n-template-bound) / [proof](#proof-stmt-n-template-bound): Count residual orbit partitions, transitive overgroups and bounded quotient subgroups. -> A computable bound independent of unit weights
- **n-circuit-template** [claim](#stmt-n-circuit-template) / [proof](#proof-stmt-n-circuit-template): Encode circuit gates through weighted total and square comparisons. -> A template whose readings recover a solution
- **n-undecidable** [claim](#stmt-n-undecidable) / [proof](#proof-stmt-n-undecidable): Use a hypothetical representation decider to bound witness carriers and hence positive circuit solutions. -> Undecidability of finite representability
- **n-interval-undecidable** [claim](#stmt-n-interval-undecidable) / [proof](#proof-stmt-n-interval-undecidable): Replace the carrier bound by a bound on top-group order in the circuit argument. -> Undecidability of subgroup-interval recognition
- **q-size-ceiling** [claim](#stmt-q-size-ceiling) / [proof](#proof-stmt-q-size-ceiling): Make the structural parameter choices computably and count the affine-chart lattice elements. -> A computable size ceiling for a negative example
- **q-minimum** [claim](#stmt-q-minimum) / [proof](#proof-stmt-q-minimum): Use the Busy Beaver witness cutoff to select the first negative table in the bounded order. -> A finite specification with proof of minimum cardinality

<a id="pm-s4"></a>
## 4. Engineering Triptych

### Panel 1 - epistemic contract

- **I_GRAPH**: A candidate witness must separate distinct vertices, reflect the lattice order, satisfy the lattice triangle inequality, and meet every edge-image reachability requirement.
- **I_BOUNDED**: Once the graph size is fixed, checking a candidate is a finite calculation.

### Panel 2 - negative knowledge

- **A_TOTAL**: Treat exhaustion of a bounded graph search as a general nonrepresentability decision. -> The chosen search limit need not reach an affirmative witness.
- **A_EMBED**: Accept an order-faithful coloring after checking only the triangle inequality. -> The admissible-map algebra may have additional congruences.

### Panel 3 - reference implementation and oracle

Applicability: `algorithmic`. The finite colored-graph criterion gives a terminating check of each fixed candidate witness. The implementation checks that finite criterion; it does not decide unrestricted representability.

```python
# INPUTS: JSON batch of {le: finite lattice order matrix, d: symmetric color matrix}.
# PRECONDITIONS: bottom index 0; 1<=|L|<=5; 1<=|A|<=3; valid lattice; zero diagonal.
# OUTPUTS: JSON booleans, true exactly for graph witnesses in this bounded domain.
# TIME: O(j^j*j^2 + 2^(j*(j+1)/2)*(j^j*j^2+j^3) + n^3).
# SPACE: O(j^j*j+n^2+j^2).
# ARITHMETIC: exact integer indices and python-flint integer subset bounds.
# FAILURE: malformed or out-of-contract input raises; false rejects only this graph.
import sys, json, itertools
from flint import fmpz

def witness(case):
    le, d = case['le'], case['d']
    n, j = len(le), len(d)
    assert 1 <= n <= 5 and 1 <= j <= 3
    assert all(len(row)==n for row in le) and all(len(row)==j for row in d)
    assert all(type(x) is int and 0<=x<n for row in d for x in row)
    assert all(d[p][p]==0 and all(d[p][q]==d[q][p] for q in range(j)) for p in range(j))
    join = {}
    for a in range(n):
        assert le[0][a] and le[a][a]
        for b in range(n):
            upper=[c for c in range(n) if le[a][c] and le[b][c]]
            least=[c for c in upper if all(le[c][v] for v in upper)]
            lower=[c for c in range(n) if le[c][a] and le[c][b]]
            assert len(least)==1 and sum(all(le[v][c] for v in lower) for c in lower)==1
            assert a==b or not(le[a][b] and le[b][a])
            assert all(not(le[a][b] and le[b][c]) or le[a][c] for c in range(n))
            join[a,b]=least[0]
    for p,q in itertools.product(range(j), repeat=2):
        if p != q and d[p][q] == 0: return False
        if any(not le[d[p][q]][join[d[p][u],d[u][q]]] for u in range(j)): return False
    for a,b in itertools.product(range(n), repeat=2):
        if not le[a][b] and not any(le[d[p][q]][a] and not le[d[p][q]][b] for p in range(j) for q in range(j)): return False
    maps=[f for f in itertools.product(range(j),repeat=j) if all(le[d[f[p]][f[q]]][d[p][q]] for p in range(j) for q in range(j))]
    edges=list(itertools.combinations_with_replacement(range(j),2))
    for mask in range(1,int(fmpz(2)**len(edges))):
        selected=[e for k,e in enumerate(edges) if mask>>k&1]
        a=0
        for p,q in selected: a=join[a,d[p][q]]
        reach=[[p==q for q in range(j)] for p in range(j)]
        for f in maps:
            for p,q in selected: reach[f[p]][f[q]]=reach[f[q]][f[p]]=True
        for u in range(j):
            for p in range(j):
                for q in range(j): reach[p][q] |= reach[p][u] and reach[u][q]
        if any(le[d[p][q]][a] and not reach[p][q] for p in range(j) for q in range(j)): return False
    return True
print(json.dumps([witness(c) for c in json.load(sys.stdin)]))
```
